title: What’s New
text: Updates and improvements to the ACC Baseball Explorer.

title: What’s New
text:
July 2026
Player Profile Pages
Added individual player profile pages for both batters and pitchers.
Users can now explore:

Multi-season performance histories
Advanced metrics including wRC+, wOBA, ISO, FIP, and K-BB%
Season-by-season percentile rankings

Percentile rankings are calculated using season-specific ACC context, allowing player performance to be evaluated relative to peers from the same year.
Downloadable Data
Added CSV downloads directly from the Explorer.
Users can now export:

Batter statistics
Pitcher statistics
Conference leaderboard data

The downloadable files match the statistics displayed in the application and allow users to perform additional analysis outside of the Explorer.
ACC Baseball Explorer Launch
The initial release of the Explorer introduced interactive tools for analyzing ACC baseball performance, including:

Advanced batting metrics
Advanced pitching metrics
Team-level comparisons
Conference visualizations

title: What’s New
text:
May 2026
accbaseballr R Package Released
Created the accbaseballr R package to provide a standardized framework for analyzing ACC baseball statistics.
The package processes raw college baseball data and calculates advanced metrics including:
wOBA wRC+ ISO FIP K-BB%
The package was submitted to and accepted by CRAN, making it publicly available to the R community.

Continued updates as new ACC baseball seasons become available

title: About the Project
text:
The ACC Baseball Explorer was created to bring modern sabermetric analysis to college baseball. While advanced metrics such as wOBA, wRC+, and FIP have become standard tools for evaluating Major League Baseball, comparable analytical resources for college baseball remain limited.
This project applies similar approaches to ACC baseball, allowing player and team performance to be evaluated in greater context through interactive tools and reproducible statistical methods.

title: About the Project
text:
Data Source
The ACC Baseball Explorer uses publicly available college baseball statistics from ACC programs dating back to 2011.
The underlying data is processed through the accbaseballr R package, which was developed specifically to calculate advanced sabermetrics metrics including:

wOBA
wRC+
ISO
K-BB%
FIP

The package standardizes raw statistics, calculates league context, and creates a consistent framework for comparing players and teams across seasons.

title: About the Project
text:
Technology
The ACC Baseball Explorer was built using:

R for data processing and statistical calculations
tidyverse for data manipulation
Shiny for the interactive web application
reactable for dynamic player and team tables
ggplot2 for data visualization
Quarto for this documentation website

title: About the Project
text:
Development
This project was built as a way to explore the application of data analytics and statistical modeling within college baseball.
The goal is to make advanced baseball analysis more accessible while providing a reproducible framework for evaluating player and team performance.

title: Advanced Analytics for ACC Baseball
text:
Built with publicly available ACC baseball data and advanced sabermetric methodology using the accbaseballr R package.
Explore ACC baseball performance through interactive visualizations, advanced metrics, percentile rankings, and downloadable data spanning seasons from 2011 to the present.
This project was created to make advanced college baseball analytics more accessible. By providing transparent methodology, interactive tools, and freely available data, the ACC Baseball Explorer helps fans, analysts, coaches, and researchers better understand player and team performance.
The ACC Baseball Explorer provides a centralized resource for analyzing conference performance from 2011-present using metrics including:

wRC+ — adjusted offensive production
wOBA — overall offensive value
ISO — power production
FIP — fielding-independent pitching performance
K-BB% — strikeout-to-walk differential

title: Metrics
text:
The ACC Baseball Explorer uses modern sabermetric statistics to evaluate player performance beyond traditional statistics such as batting average, RBI, and ERA.
These metrics provide additional context by accounting for league environment, offensive value, and outcomes that are more directly controlled by the player.





Weighted On-Base Average measures a hitter’s total offensive value per plate appearance by assigning specific run values to events like walks, singles, doubles, triples, and home runs.
\[
wOBA = \frac{0.69*BB + 0.72*HBP + 0.89*1B + 1.27*2B + 1.62*3B + 2.10* HR}{AB + BB + HBP + SF}
\] where:

BB = Bases on Balls/Walks
HBP = Times Hit by a Pitch
1B = Singles hit
2B = Doubles hit
3B = Triples hit
HR = Home Runs hit
AB = At Bats
SF = Sacrifice Flies




Weighted Runs Created Plus measures a batter’s total offensive value and run creation per plate appearance, adjusted for league run environments.
\[
wRC+ = \left(\frac{wOBA - wOBA_{league}}{scale} + 1 \right) * 100
\] where:

wOBAleague = league-average wOBA calculated from all player plate appearances during the season
scale = wOBA scale factor used to normalize differences in offensive value (1.25)

Interpretation

100 = league average
120 = 20% above league average
80 = 20% below league average

Higher values indicate stronger offensive performance.



Isolated Power measures a batter’s raw power by calculating how many extra-base hits they average per at-bat.
\[
SLG - BA
\] where:

SLG = Slugging Percentage
**BA* = Batting Average




Batting Average on Balls in Play measures how often a batted ball becomes a hit while excluding home runs and strikeouts.
\[
BABIP = \frac{H - HR}{AB - SO - HR + SF}
\] where:

H = Hits
HR = Home Runs hit
AB = At Bats
SO = Strikeouts
SF = Sacrifice Flies








K-BB% measures a pitcher’s control by subtracting total walks (BB) from total strikeouts (SO).
\[
K-BB% = K% - BB%
\] where:
-K% = Strikeouts divided by batters faced -BB% = Bases on Balls/Walks divided by batters faced



Fielding Independent Pitching measures a pitcher’s true performance by focusing only on the events a pitcher has the most control over.
\[
FIP = \frac{13*HR + 3*(BB + HBP) - 2*SO}{IP} + 3.10
\] where:

HR = Home Runs allowed
BB = Bases on Balls/Walks
HBP = Times Hit by a Pitch
SO = Strikeouts
IP = Innings Pitched

3.10 is used as a constant to approximate a standard Earned Run Average (ERA) scale.
Interpretation
Lower FIP values indicate better pitching performance.

All metrics are calculated using the accbaseballr R package developed for ACC baseball analysis.
